### 2026-10-14: It's my first time working with Onshape, so I had to create a new account. Then it took a while to learn all the viewport navigations via Youtube videos. However, I was able to do it. The process of m

**5h**

It's my first time working with Onshape, so I had to create a new account. Then it took a while to learn all the viewport navigations via Youtube videos. However, I was able to do it. The process of making a sketch and shapes was interesting to point that the actual process of making my first track took less time that the time to learn, because I wanted to know how to make things. I'm also going to make a new document and creating cool shapes as drafts for my runway.

### 2026-10-16: I had created my first document, but now I had to create a new document, because I somehow glitched the system by creating too large of a fillet and I couldn’t remove it. So I had to spend some time f

**10h**

I had created my first document, but now I had to create a new document, because I somehow glitched the system by creating too large of a fillet and I couldn’t remove it. So I had to spend some time fixing the problem. It turns out all I had to do was select then DRAG. The guide wasn't clear on that, but I guess that's a part of the problem solving process :p. But the good news is that I managed to finally create my fillet. I continued on to make the fillet the correct geometry as in radius and this time I also managed to take more screenshots of the process. I will now continue on to making lines and circles, I am half way there to creating my actual runway.

**5h**

This is it, the final product. I practiced making curves and how to create composite curves and angle sketches to create correct oriented tracks. I also added pillars to keep the tracks up for more stability as in standard practices, people often add these structural supports to make printing easier.
